title: Memoize `MacroReflection#klass` for self-referential associations
body:
### Motivation / Background

`MacroReflection#_klass` memoizes the resolved class with `@klass ||= begin ... end`, but `return` inside the `begin` block exits the method before the assignment takes place. This means self-referential associations — where the `demodulize` branch is taken — skip the memoization on every call:

```ruby
class Comment < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :parent, class_name: "Comment"
  has_many :children, class_name: "Comment"
end

reflection = Comment.reflect_on_association(:parent)
reflection.klass
reflection.instance_variable_get(:@klass) #=> nil (expected: Comment)
```

`klass` resolves the constant again on every call (association reads, builds, preloading, scope resolution), and `Reflection#freeze` does not warm the class as intended.

### Detail

Replace `return` with a local variable so the value flows through the `begin` block and is properly assigned to `@klass`. A regression test asserts that `compute_class` is only called once across repeated `klass` calls.

### Additional information

Rough micro-benchmark (100k `klass` calls, sqlite3):

| reflection | per call | allocations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `belongs_to :post` | 0.05 µs | 0 |
| `belongs_to :parent, class_name: "Comment"` | 0.53 µs | 1 |

With this change both take the memoized path.
